test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which dance from Assam involves a group of dancers performing in circles or rows, often accompanied by drums and pipes, to celebrate the Bihu festival?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bihu** is a traditional dance form of Assam, performed during the **Bihu festival**, which is one of the most significant cultural celebrations in the region.
 
• The dance is characterized by its **lively movements**, performed in circles or rows, and is accompanied by traditional instruments like **drums (dhol), pipes (pepa), and cymbals (toka).**
 
• The Bihu festival marks the **Assamese New Year** and is celebrated to express gratitude for a good harvest and to welcome the spring season.
 
• This dance involves **vigorous hand and foot movements**, reflecting the joy and energy of the festival, and is performed by both men and women, wearing traditional Assamese attire.
 
• Bihu dance is a symbol of Assamese culture and heritage and has gained recognition both nationally and internationally for its **vibrant and energetic performances.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bagurumba:**

 
 
• Bagurumba is a folk dance of the **Bodo community** in Assam.
 
• It is also known as the **butterfly dance** due to its graceful movements resembling a butterfly's flight.
 
• Performed by Bodo women, this dance is often associated with nature and is typically performed during the **Bwisagu festival**.
 
 
 
• **Dhol Cholom:**
 
 
• Dhol Cholom is a traditional dance from **Manipur**, performed during the festival of **Holi**.
 
• This dance involves vigorous drumming on the dhol and synchronized movements by performers, showcasing their **strength and rhythm.**
 
• It is not associated with the Bihu festival or Assamese culture.
 
 
 
• **Hojagiri:**
 
 
• Hojagiri is a traditional dance of the **Reang (Bru) tribe** of Tripura.
 
• This dance is performed by women balancing earthen pots on their heads and showcasing intricate footwork and movements.
 
• It is distinct from the Bihu dance and is associated with the **Hojagiri festival**.
 
 
 
• **Bihu Festival:**
 
 
• The Bihu festival is celebrated in three forms: **Bohag Bihu** (spring), **Magh Bihu** (harvest), and **Kati Bihu** (sowing).
 
• It is a time of **feasting, dancing, and singing**, reflecting the cultural and agricultural heritage of Assam.
 
• The traditional attire includes **mekhela chador** for women and dhoti-gamosa for men.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Bihu dance is performed during **Bohag Bihu**, which is celebrated in April and marks the beginning of the Assamese New Year.
 
• The dance is an integral part of the festivities, symbolizing joy, prosperity, and the vibrant spirit of the Assamese people.
 
• It has been recognized as a **representation of India’s rich cultural diversity** on various platforms, including international cultural festivals.
 
• Assamese musical instruments like the **pepa** (a wind instrument made from buffalo horn) and the **dhol** play a pivotal role in the performance, adding to its energy and rhythm.
